channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Cindy Holscher wins in Kansas, holding governor's office for Democrats
item.description: Holscher, a state senator, overcame a more well-known Republican who had Trump's endorsement in the state that has gone to the GOP in most other statewide races.

item.title: US soldier accused of spying for Russia identified: Source
item.description: US officer who was arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia is 41-year-old Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, according to a source familiar with the investigation.

item.title: Timeline of the stunning fall of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: While the depths of the scandal have yet to be disclosed, here is a timeline indicating who knew what and when about Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

item.title: Eight killed, including two children, in New York building collapse
item.description: Eight people, including two children, were killed when a residential building collapsed into an adjacent construction site in Brooklyn on Wednesday. Firefighters spent hours searching the rubble overnight before declaring the operation over on Thursday, as authorities launched an investigation into the disaster.

item.title: What's a Honey Trap? The spy tactic that helped topple Jensen Huang
item.description: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, the leading AI chipmaker, resigned after admitting an extramarital affair with a woman the U.S. says is a Chinese spy. This espionage tactic is known as a honey trap.

item.title: Donald Trump Jr. exits advisory role at prediction market Kalshi
item.description: Donald Trump Jr. is no longer a paid adviser for Kalshi, the prediction market company said Thursday

item.title: Russia using 'illegal and unethical means, knows Europe won't use same means back', expert says
item.description: There are mounting concerns across Europe that recent hoax threats and cyber attacks could be part of a massive hybrid warfare campaign. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Elisabeth Braw, Senior Fellow with the Atlantic Council’s Transatlantic Security Initiative. She says that Russia's aim is to "increase its power at the expense of European countries and the easiest way to do that is to constantly wage this dirty war against European countries, using illegal and unethical means, because Russia knows that we are not going to use the same means back".

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after mounting scandals
item.description: Jensen Huang, long considered the face of the AI revolution, has resigned as Nvidia's President, CEO and board member as sandals over his romantic affairs wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the company's market value in a matter of days. US lawmakers signal they'll likely push for tighter export restrictions for AI chips. Meanwhile, the rapid buildout of AI data centre is sparking anger and worries among French communities.

item.title: Mauritania fishing boats falsely portrayed as migrant fleet bound for Spain
item.description: Spain’s Canary Islands are facing renewed pressure from migrant arrivals, with local authorities declaring a state of emergency. Against this backdrop, a viral video claims to show thousands of boats in Mauritania amassing at the port, that users said was "ready to set sail" to carry migrants to the archipelago. But the satellite images are misleading: they show a traditional fishing port, not a fleet of migrant vessels. Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.

item.title: Colom’s historic Senate win could reshape Mississippi’s political future: Analysis
item.description: The question is whether his victory can establish a lasting realignment.

item.title: WATCH: How Mississippi Sen.-elect Scott Colom's win is 145 years in the making
item.description: ABC News' Faith Abuby details the historic win of Mississippi Sen.-elect Scott Colom as the state's first Democrat to win a Senate seat since 1982 and the first Black senator since Reconstruction.

item.title: Across Africa: Tunisians drawn into Russia's war with Ukraine
item.description: This week: A new report says more than 1,400 Africans have been recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine since 2023. Also, as South Africa races to become Africa's digital gateway, a growing backlash is emerging in Cape Town. And music, dance and theatre lit up Abéché as the city's arts festival in Chad drew crowds of young spectators.

item.title: Outlook outage: Microsoft reports 'issues' with Teams and email
item.description: Microsoft is reporting "issues" with users accessing Outlook and Teams.

item.title: Ngo criticizes UN's response to massacre in South Sudan
item.description: In tonight's edition, Amnesty International accuses both the government and UN peacekeepers of failing to protect civilians during a massacre in South Sudan that killed over 200 people. Also, more than a thousand people are prosecuted for illegal mining in Guinea. And a century after French colonial troops killed him, a Malagasy king has finally come home.

item.title: 'There's no such thing as safe' in contact sports, brain injury expert says
item.description: Discussing the issue of contact sports and the threat to sports men and women of all ages, particularly in the light of the recent death, just last month, of a 17-year-old French woman after a head collision on the rugby field, FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Dr Daniel H Daneshvar, Associate Professor at Harvard Medical School. He says that "there's not such thing as safe" in contact sports, explaining that "if you get a lot of repeated hits to the head, then you're at risk for problems later in life, both in the near term and the long term".

item.title: Mechanic offered 'special serum' to man who drugged and raped wife, court hears
item.description: A mechanic accused of plotting to drug and rape a man's wife offered a "special serum" to make her unconscious, a court has heard.

item.title: Republicans push for Jensen Huang's testimony following Nvidia CEO's resignation
item.description: "I don't think he's got anything to hide now. Let it fly," Rep. Burchett said.

item.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six, including surgeon, medics say
item.description: Israeli fire killed 11 people in Gaza on Thursday, six of them in the bombing of Nasser hospital in south Gaza early in the day, health officials said, the deadliest single strike since Israel's elections last month. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Dr Goher Rahbour, a surgeon working at the Nasser Hospital.

item.title: Zelensky warns Europe over US-Russia talks on broader security arrangements
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned European leaders Thursday to be wary of discussions between the United States and Russia about a new security arrangement for the continent. Before launching the war in 2022, the Kremlin delivered an ultimatum to NATO on Europe's security arrangements which included demands for the alliance to withdraw forces from eastern Europe and stop accepting new members. FRANCE 24's Caroline Baum reports.

item.title: Plugged-in planet? COP31 host Turkey leads charge for electrification
item.description: It’s sweater weather in Paris. But even though November brings brisk temperatures and fall foliage, it doesn’t mean last summer’s record heat should fade from our memories. One of the suggested reasons why students are so boiling mad is the hell they endured back in June in overheated classrooms and baking shoebox apartments.

item.title: White House reportedly discussing Howard Lutnick's future as Commerce secretary
item.description: Senior White House officials are discussing whether ​Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should be pushed out in the wake of the spy scandal surrounding Nvidia's now ​former ‌CEO Jensen Huang, two people familiar ⁠with the situation told Reuters on Thursday. In June, Reuters reported that the Trump administration had held ⁠off from adding China’s AI startup DeepSeek, memory chipmaker CXMT and more than 100 other companies flagged as national security risks to a trade blacklist. FRANCE 24's Wassim Cornet reports from Los Angeles.

item.title: Men who raped teenager are on the run after skipping trial
item.description: Two men convicted of raping a teenage girl who was groomed and trafficked in Rotherham 20 years ago are on the run.

item.title: Winter is coming: Putin seeks to 'hammer Ukrainians, their power grid, their water supplies'
item.description: As renewed diplomatic efforts seek to bring an end to Russia's war on Ukraine, the prospect of a negotiated settlement remains unlikely due to Russia's irreconcilable territorial demands, competing visions of European security and an increasingly unpredictable and pro-Moscow American approach to mediation. For Russia expert Mark Galeotti, Executive Director of Mayak Intelligence and Honorary Professor at University College London's School of Slavonic and East European Studies, Moscow's maximalist vision conceals a more complex negotiating strategy. "The Russian approach is always to sound incredibly bullish and then make any concessions at the very last minute," he explains, suggesting that the Kremlin's uncompromising rhetoric should not necessarily be mistaken for an absolute refusal to negotiate. Yet the territorial dispute over Donbas presents a particularly formidable obstacle. Putin's determination to claim control over the entirety of the region confronts Ukraine's refusal to su

item.title: 'Punch in the gut': Homes sales fall to their lowest in 16 years
item.description: Existing homes sales in October declined 8.8% from a year earlier, according to the National Association of Realtors.

item.title: Soldier who admonished Hegseth group at Arlington Cemetery awarded a medal
item.description: The incident occurred after a group photo at the Tomb of the Unknowns.

item.title: Harry Kane marks record England cap with a goal at Wembley
item.description: Harry Kane has become England's most-capped men's footballer, scoring in a 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley.

item.title: Israel to ban far-left French politician Jean-Luc Mélenchon from entry
item.description: The Israeli government said Thursday that it would ban far-left French leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon from entering the country after the French presidential contender said he would use French vessels to force aid into Gaza if he were elected. The announcement comes a day after France confirmed it had refused entry to the head of a body representing settlements in the occupied West Bank.

item.title: ‘Labelled terrorists’: How France is using anti-terror powers to deter protests
item.description: The French government has been accused of weaponising an anti-terror law adopted in the wake of the 2015 Paris attacks to keep dozens of people away from massive protests sweeping the country. Lawyers and rights groups denounce an abuse of power with potentially dangerous repercussions for individual liberties and the right to protest.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?
item.description: As Trump's arch and other projects make their way through the courts, many critics are looking to Congress to stop them. Democrats have a few tools, including funding and oversight.

item.title: Concentration of power & wealth: Do tech CEOs have more authority, influence than elected officials?
item.description: The resignation of Nvidia founder Jensen Huang has thrown one of the world's most iconic technology companies into a leadership crisis, whose ripple effects extend far beyond Silicon Valley. Nvidia occupies a unique position in a booming AI industruy marked by intensifying competition between the United States and China. Its leadership upheaval raises immediate questions about corporate succession. But it is also fueling a broader debate about economic resilience, national security and the political influence of big tech titans. For Gavin Bade, trade and economic policy reporter at The Wall Street Journal, the controversy illustrates the extraordinary concentration of economic power in a handful of corporations and the individuals who lead them. “Do these CEOs actually have more authority and more influence than our elected officials?”

item.title: Russia's Vladimir Putin suggests no Ukraine compromise in meeting with US envoys
item.description: Russia's President Vladimir Putin indicated on Thursday, November 12, that the Kremlin would not compromise on its hardline demands to end the war in Ukraine, but offered a short-term ceasefire in a key frontline city during a meeting with US envoys. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.

item.title: Iran live updates: 'We don't need a deal with Iran,' Trump says
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: The SS United States takes its final voyage to the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico
item.description: A ship bigger than the Titanic is being sunk off the coast of Florida to make an artificial reef.

item.title: Israel kills six in Gaza hospital strike as 9-month-old baby freezes to death
item.description: An overnight Israeli air strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza killed at least six Palestinians Thursday, including a teenage boy and a surgeon, medics said. Elsewhere in the devastated Palestinian territory, a nine-month-old baby died from the cold as families flee worsening flooding.

item.title: Witnesses describe the D.C. shooting that left 1 dead, 4 injured
item.description: A gunman opened fire at a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle Thursday morning. One person has been confirmed killed and four others injured. The gunman is dead, according to police.

item.title: Teenage girl who stabbed love rival to death pleads guilty to murder
item.description: A teenager who stabbed another girl to death during a pre-planned fight over a boy has pleaded guilty to murder.

item.title: ICE reports record immigration arrests, deportations since Trump White House return
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history

item.title: How FRANCE 24 traced Tehran-backed Afghan fighters from Syria to southeastern Iran
item.description: Members of the Tehran-backed Afghan Shia militia known as the Fatemiyoun division have resurfaced in Iran after largely disappearing from public view following the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s government in Syria in 2024. FRANCE 24 used "martyrdom” announcements and the geolocation of videos shared on social media to trace their presence.

item.title: At least five people shot in DC neighbourhood near the White House
item.description: At least one person died after five people were shot early Thursday in a Washington, DC neighbourhood near the White House, police said. A swarm of officers responded to a nearby apartment building where a suspect was barricaded and later shot himself.

item.title: Life through a lens: Celebrating 200 years of photography
item.description: A passport photo, a selfie, an award-winning film and even the evening news: all of them were made possible thanks to a "fantastic machine", the camera. As France celebrates the bicentenary of the first fixed photographic image, we discuss the image-obsessed society we live in with filmmaker Maximilien Van Aertryck and artist Alina Frieske.

item.title: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth reprimanded at war memorial
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, along with his wife and aides, was silenced by a guard on Wednesday at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Hegseth's group was at Arlington National Cemetery for a Veterans Day ceremony when they were reprimanded for laughing and taking pictures in front of the sombre memorial.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after revelations on extramarital affairs
item.description: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of AI giant Nvidia on Thursday, November 12, after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Washington Fraser Jackson and FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert have more.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns, in a spectacular downfall for the longtime head of the chipmaker, a vital player in the artificial intelligence boom. The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion-dollar company plunging, and the exit of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom, leaves Nvidia without its leather-jacket-clad leader at a crucial time for the sector.

item.title: WATCH: United Airlines banning AI bots from booking flights
item.description: The airline says customers who give their personal and credit card information to AI businesses run the risk of having their sensitive data exposed.

item.title: WATCH: Pope Leo returns to Peru for historic visit
item.description: The visit marks Pope Leo’s first return to the country where he served as a missionary and bishop for nearly two decades.

item.title: U.S. envoys meet with Putin in the Kremlin after Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff went to the Kremlin to brief Russian President Vladimir Putin and are scheduled to fly later to Ireland for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

item.title: WATCH: SS United States intentionally sunk off the Gulf Coast of Florida
item.description: The SS United States was lowered to its final resting place off the Florida Panhandle and will now serve as a diving destination and habitat for marine life.

item.title: Witkoff and Kushner arrive in Moscow to meet with Putin, discuss Ukraine peace talks
item.description: President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner landed in Moscow on Thursday morning.

item.title: Democrat Colom flips Mississippi Senate seat
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom will win the election for U.S. Senate in Mississippi, The Associated Press projects.

item.title: Judges consider submissions in bid for private prosecution of former footballer
item.description: A panel of judges are considering a bid to privately prosecute former Scotland striker David Goodwillie and hope to issue a ruling "as soon as practicable".

item.title: Indonesia's VP resigns as his eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
item.description: Raka is the son of former President Joko Widodo. The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents that Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements.

item.title: Man shot dead in Washington DC gym is named
item.description: A man shot dead in a Washington DC gym on Thursday has been named.

item.title: WATCH: ABC's Bob Woodruff's foundation honors wounded soldiers and their families
item.description: David Muir speaks with "The Resilient" – a band made up of wounded soldiers – backstage at Bob Woodruff's annual Stand Up for Heroes, raising millions for veterans and military families.

item.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six, health ministry says
item.description: An Israeli airstrike on a Palestinian hospital has killed at least six and wounded 28, Gaza's Health Ministry said.

item.title: WATCH: Mom becomes first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a Canadian ultramarathoner becoming the first woman ever to run 100 continuous miles in Antarctica.

item.title: Bomb alert at Calais train station disrupts Eurostar
item.description: A bomb alert at a French train station disrupted journeys including international travel, with Eurostar trains among those affected.

item.title: Poundland secures extended deadline for possible rescue
item.description: Crisis-hit Poundland has secured an extended deadline for a potential rescue amid political pressure for a solvent sale of the chain.

item.title: Fiery clashes erupt in Spain as millions join general strike
item.description: Unrest broke out in cities across Spain on Wednesday after millions of workers joined the country's first general strike in 14 years.

item.title: WATCH: President Trump pays tribute to veterans
item.description: President Donald Trump spoke at a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery honoring fallen soldiers and addressed the war with Iran.

item.title: Pope ends Argentina visit with unity plea after pushing back against Milei's agenda
item.description: Pope Leo closed an emotional visit to Argentina with an appeal for unity and reconciliation, offering a message of hope to his predecessor's polarised homeland.

item.title: WATCH: Little girl rescued after sneaker wave pulls her into Pacific
item.description: The rescue was caught on camera after a child was nearly swept out to sea by a sneaker wave along the Pacific coast.

item.title: WATCH: Blockbuster NFL trades
item.description: ABC News’ Lara Spencer has details on the big trades, including Kirk Cousins heading to the Minnesota Vikings.

item.title: WATCH: Superhero window washers make children’s day at Omaha hospital
item.description: Patients at Children’s Nebraska were surprised by superheroes washing their windows as part of a special tradition.

item.title: WATCH: NYC tour helicopter makes hard landing in New Jersey
item.description: The pilot of a New York City sightseeing helicopter is being praised for pulling off a remarkable emergency landing in Bayonne, New Jersey, after the chopper’s tail rotor broke off.

item.description: On Veterans Day, ABC News' Danny New talks to two cheerleaders for the Philadelphia Eagles who've also served their country.

item.description: ABC News’ Chief Meteorologist Ginger Zee has some eye-opening demonstrations she hopes can help save lives during flash floods.
